VIRTUAL MIDPOINTS: CONTINUOUS-TIME INFORMATION THAT SAMPLING HIDES
Solo construction, 31 October 2026. Historical priority unestablished.

1. THE MISSING OPERATION AND ITS CONTRACT

The complete discrete-time inference framework in entropy_witnesses/PROOF.txt
recovers a discrete hidden-model minimum. It does not impose continuous-time
embeddability. That limitation can erase ALL inferable dissipation: Section5
constructs a driven finite CTMC whose sampled binary process is itself an
exactly reversible Markov chain. Its discrete hidden-model minimum is zero.

Here the additional premise is stationary, time-homogeneous, reciprocal,
all-even finite CTMC dynamics, observed through a fixed binary state label
at equal physical intervals Delta. Neither its generator, hidden state count,
stationary probabilities nor mixing rate is supplied to inference. Stationary
hidden preparation and the physical time/reversal model remain external.
The target is realised FULL path entropy through N Delta, not a stationary
ensemble mean rate. Astra N185's mean-rate obstruction remains intact.

Only Y_0,...,Y_N are acquired. Let f(0)=+1,f(1)=-1 and
S_N=sum_{k<N}f(Y_k)f(Y_{k+1}). The result below uses the existence of the
hidden half-interval kernel R=exp(Delta Q/2), without observing midpoints.
More generally it applies to a stationary Markov square-root realization;
the full CTMC entropy follows by conditional Holder under path projection.

2. A RETURNING TWO-PHASE KERNEL LEMMA

Adjoin an auxiliary bit c which flips at every HALF step. Its stationary
law is uniform, its flip is a reversible involution, and its entropy is zero.
The product chain has stationary law pi times uniform and transition R times
flip. Let K be its positive entropy-tilted kernel for a bounded payoff H
satisfying the entropy cone H_s+phi*(H_a)<=0, phi(t)=2t atanh t.
The earlier proved kernel lemma gives w(K)<=exp(theta^2 M^2/2), |H_a|<=M,
for0<theta<=1/2, where w is the complex numerical radius.

The observation protocol fixes c_0=0. This initial clock law is not stationary,
but there is NO factor2 loss at an EVEN horizon: K^(2N) preserves clock phase.
For the unit vector v0=sqrt2*1{c=0} in L2(pi times uniform),

 E_{pi,c0=0} exp{theta[sum H-Sigma_halfgrid]}
      =<v0,K^(2N)v0><=w(K^(2N))<=w(K)^(2N).                (V1)

The last step is the numerical-radius power inequality already proved in
reversible_cur
